name: SubstrateMapBase
description: Abstract, non-placeable shell for substrate-map style controls: template root, canvas, devicePixelRatio bitmap sizing, ResizeObserver, one engine instance and the render request path. Declares no attributes and no events; concrete subclasses own those.

dependencyFiles.name: ../../Helpers/SubstrateMapEngine/Engine.js
dependencyFiles.description: Shared SubstrateMapEngine library. Registered here so the project webserver serves it and preloads it; the ES module cache guarantees a single evaluation even though SubstrateMapBase.js imports the same file.

dependencyFiles.name: SubstrateMapBase.js
dependencyFiles.description: Contains all the main logic as ES module.

functions.name: readEmptyState
functions.description: Which of the four empty states this control is in: 'data' when real data is bound, 'stale' when a last known state is shown with an age label, 'demo' when the demo is drawn, 'nodata' when the no-data image is. REAL DATA means something to draw - a grid with cells, or items - so a bound document that produced nothing answers 'nodata', and an outline alone does too, because an empty substrate body is a frame around nothing. Useful for driving a surrounding layout from what the control is actually showing rather than from what was bound to it.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-no-data-image
attributes.description: Image shown when the control has nothing to show. Any format the browser renders; null uses the shipped NoData.svg. Scaled to CONTAIN the drawing area and centered - an image whose aspect ratio differs from the area's is letterboxed, never stretched. Recommended at least 512 px on the long edge at a ratio near 6:5, because the shipped SVG is 252 x 213.3 and a raster rendered larger than its own size looks soft on a 4K panel. WHEN it is shown is decided by the precedence in the README: real data wins, then a last known state, then the demo, then this.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-no-data-image-dark
attributes.description: The same image for the Base-Dark theme; null uses the shipped dark variant. A separate file rather than a CSS filter, because filter: invert() rotates hue and turns a blue accent orange, while the shipped variant mirrors lightness in OKLCH and keeps every hue.

attributes.name: data-tchmi-no-data-text
attributes.description: One line under the no-data image. null draws no line at all rather than an empty one, so a control that says nothing occupies no vertical space for it.
